hero.purpose: The single largest text in the system — play.html's in-game loading title only.

display.purpose: Loading-screen and hero panel titles, rendered in solid DreamBricks Blue.

title.purpose: Card titles, totem names, button labels.

caption.purpose: Secondary descriptive text — QR captions, form hints, session meta.

label.purpose: Field labels, tab labels, uppercase Poppins.

mono-label.purpose: Panel titles, queue headers, status badges.

micro.purpose: Floor of the scale — queue-row device meta, ETA text, timestamp chips. Always paired with an icon or adjacent larger text.

shadows.name: card-lift
shadows.purpose: QR card and single-focus panels animating into view.

shadows.name: modal-lift
shadows.purpose: Modal content over the dimmed/blurred overlay.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default transition for hover/active state changes across buttons and cards.

motion.name: ease-modal
motion.purpose: Modal fade-in and QR card slide-up entrance.

motion.name: reveal-in
motion.purpose: Logo-mark entrance on loading/queue screens — ease-out fade+scale, not bounce/elastic.

motion.name: pulse-live
motion.purpose: Ambient 'live' status dot in the operator header — the one resting-state animation in the system.

motion.name: gamepad-press
motion.purpose: Face/D-pad button press feedback — tuned fast for thumb input.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Main call-to-action across the operator dashboard (Salvar Totem, Adicionar Totem).
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #42b0d5; color: #fff; font-family: 'Poppins', sans-serif; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 700; padding: 13px 18px; border: none; border-radius: 10px; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 0.2s, box-shadow 0.2s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); box-shadow: 0 4px 14px oklch(from #42b0d5 l c h / 0.4); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #52cdef; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(0); } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.4; cursor: not-allowed; transform: none; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Cancel / dismiss actions inside modals and forms.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: oklch(0.94 0.010 230); color: oklch(0.52 0.022 230); border: 1px solid oklch(0.89 0.014 230); font-family: 'Poppins', sans-serif; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 700; padding: 9px 14px; border-radius: 10px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s, color 0.2s; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: oklch(0.89 0.014 230); color: oklch(0.16 0.028 230); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #52cdef; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Standard text/number/select field used across totem and session forms.
components.css: .ds-input { background: oklch(0.94 0.010 230); border: 1px solid oklch(0.89 0.014 230); color: oklch(0.16 0.028 230); font-family: 'Poppins', sans-serif; font-size: 15px; padding: 11px 14px; border-radius: 10px; width: 100%; outline: none; transition: border-color 0.2s, box-shadow 0.2s; } .ds-input:focus { border-color: #42b0d5; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px oklch(from #42b0d5 l c h / 0.18); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: oklch(0.52 0.022 230); opacity: 0.7; }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Semantic status pill (active/finished/waiting/live) used on session cards and the QR panel.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; font-family: 'Poppins', sans-serif; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.5px; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 2px 10px; border-radius: 999px; } .ds-badge--success { background: oklch(0.62 0.14 155 / 0.12); color: oklch(0.62 0.14 155); border: 1px solid oklch(0.62 0.14 155 / 0.3); } .ds-badge--danger { background: oklch(0.58 0.20 25 / 0.12); color: oklch(0.58 0.20 25); border: 1px solid oklch(0.58 0.20 25 / 0.3); }

components.name: Session Card
components.description: Individual live-session card in the operator dashboard grid.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid oklch(0.89 0.014 230); border-radius: 10px; padding: 20px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 0.2s, transform 0.2s; } .ds-card:hover { border-color: #42b0d5; transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-card-id { font-size: 13px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; color: oklch(0.52 0.022 230); } .ds-card-players { font-size: 14px; color: oklch(0.52 0.022 230); } .ds-card-players strong { color: oklch(0.16 0.028 230); }

components.name: Gamepad Face Button
components.description: The signature ABXY face button — Xbox palette, skeuomorphic key-press shadow, tuned for thumb input on the player's phone. Explicitly excluded from the DreamBricks brand migration (Xbox Quarantine Rule).
components.css: .ds-face-btn { border-radius: 50%; border: none; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 60px; height: 60px; font-size: 20px; font-weight: 700; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: 0 5px 0 oklch(0.16 0.028 230 / 0.15); transition: transform 0.08s, box-shadow 0.08s, filter 0.08s; } .ds-face-btn--a { background: #107c10; color: #fff; } .ds-face-btn:active, .ds-face-btn.pressed { transform: scale(0.87) translateY(3px); box-shadow: 0 2px 0 oklch(0.16 0.028 230 / 0.15); filter: brightness(1.35); }

components.name: Live Status Dot
components.description: Ambient pulsing dot in the operator header signaling the dashboard is live-connected — the one resting-state animation in the system.
components.css: .ds-badge-live { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; font-family: 'Poppins', sans-serif; font-size: 13px; color: oklch(0.62 0.14 155); font-weight: 600; } .ds-dot-pulse { width: 8px; height: 8px; background: oklch(0.62 0.14 155); border-radius: 50%; animation: ds-pulse 2s ease-in-out infinite; } @keyframes ds-pulse { 0%, 100% { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1); } 50% { opacity: 0.4; transform: scale(0.7); } }

narrative.northStar: The Control Room, on DreamBricks Blue
narrative.overview:
Street Arcade is built on the DreamBricks Design System — DreamBricks' own brand tokens — merged with the arcade-specific signature this product depends on: monospace labels for anything that is live system data, and the Xbox-style ABXY button palette on the gamepad. The base layer reads like an instrument panel wearing the DreamBricks brand: light, blue-tinted slate surfaces, thin 1px borders, and a single confident accent (DreamBricks Blue) doing all the 'this is interactive' signaling. The playful half of the brand doesn't come from decoration; it comes from the Xbox-style button palette on the gamepad and the pulsing live dot in the operator header. Reliable first, playful second, exactly as PRODUCT.md states.

This system explicitly rejects both of PRODUCT.md's anti-references: it is not a gray enterprise SaaS panel, and it is not neon/cyberpunk gamer aesthetic. Saturated color is spent deliberately on the few places it earns its keep: buttons, badges, and the four gamepad face buttons.

The DreamBricks brandbook is a generic 'project dashboard' brand with no gamepad or real-time-queue guidance of its own. Street Arcade adopts its color/type/radius tokens wholesale for the base chrome, but keeps the Xbox gamepad palette and the mono-for-live-data rule (now carried by DreamBricks' own IBM Plex Mono token) as the two elements PRODUCT.md treats as essential and the DreamBricks system has no answer for.
keyCharacteristics: Light, blue-tinted slate base (oklch(0.97 0.006 230)) with white surface cards, never dark-mode-by-default
One accent color (DreamBricks Blue #42b0d5) carrying all primary CTAs, focus states, and active-tab indicators
IBM Plex Mono reserved for anything that reads as data or a system label; Poppins for everything conversational
Flat surfaces at rest; shadows and glow appear only as a response to hover, focus, or an open modal — tinted with Ink, never pure black
Saturated color bursts are scoped tightly: session status badges, the Xbox-palette gamepad buttons, the pulsing live dot — never the base chrome

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: DreamBricks Blue is the only color allowed to mean 'primary action' or 'focused/active.' If a second action needs color, it borrows CTA Orange — never a second blue, never a gradient invented on the spot.

rules.name: The Xbox Quarantine Rule
rules.body: The Xbox four-color palette exists only inside the gamepad's face buttons. It never appears on a badge, a button in the dashboard, or a status indicator.

rules.name: The Data-Is-Mono Rule
rules.body: Any value that represents live or identifying system state — session IDs, player IDs, timers, IPs, ports, queue positions — renders in IBM Plex Mono, regardless of its surrounding context.

rules.name: The Flat-Until-Touched Rule
rules.body: Nothing in the system has a resting shadow except the gamepad's face buttons (which are simulating physical keys, not UI chrome). If you're adding a shadow to something that isn't hovered, focused, pressed, or animating in, remove it.

dos: Do keep the base UI light and flat — Slate Background, Surface White cards, 1px Border Slate dividers, no shadow at rest.
Do reserve IBM Plex Mono for live/system data (IDs, timers, statuses, panel titles) and Poppins for everything else.
Do let DreamBricks Blue carry every primary action and focus state; introduce a second color only through the semantic Success/Danger/Warning set or CTA Orange, never a new blue.
Do confine the Xbox four-color palette to the gamepad's face buttons — it is the product's signature moment precisely because it doesn't appear anywhere else.
Do tint every shadow with Ink (oklch(0.16 0.028 230)), never pure black.
Do use shadow and glow only as a response to interaction (hover, focus, press, modal-open) — never as static decoration.
Do keep motion purposeful and quick (0.15–0.4s transitions, the 2s ambient pulse dot) — arcade energy shows up as responsiveness, not ornament.
donts: Don't build a gray, dense, enterprise-admin-panel screen — per PRODUCT.md, this should never read as generic SaaS.
Don't reach for neon gradients, RGB glow, glitch effects, or a dark-mode-by-default theme — per PRODUCT.md, this should never read as gamer/cyberpunk aesthetic.
Don't use background-clip: text gradients anywhere — loading/hero titles render in solid DreamBricks Blue; emphasis comes from weight and size.
Don't add a resting shadow to a card, button, or badge that isn't hovered, focused, pressed, or animating in.
Don't introduce a second accent blue, a new gradient, or an off-palette status color — Success, Danger, Warning, DreamBricks Blue, and CTA Orange are the complete semantic set.
Don't let the Xbox button palette leak into dashboard badges, tabs, or any non-gamepad control.
Don't reach for Fira Code or Fira Sans in new work — both fonts have been fully retired in favor of the DreamBricks IBM Plex Mono / Poppins pair.
